chk.text: Konda, lord of Eiganjo, pulls an aspect of O-Kagachi through a veil weakened by the Apocalypse Chime, and in doing so begins the Kami War.
His adviser Hisoka warns him against the war because it cannot be won, and his general Takeno recalls forces from the Takenuma Swamp because of daily losses to kami attacks.

His daughter Michiko leaves her father's fortress to consult holy monks and the orochi about the kami's rage, and in the war's twentieth year she frees the scion Kyodai and defeats both O-Kagachi and Konda.

bok.text: Konda grows suspicious that unseen hands are manipulating even his most loyal allies, and his fear deepens as the war goes badly.
He falls ill with fever and sees a spirit-child offering a way to make his empire last forever, and he orders Takeno to find Isao.

Hisoka asks what will be written on their graves, and then O-Kagachi descends on Eiganjo Castle and ruins it, while Toshiro Umezawa steals the Taken One from Konda's sanctum, and the kami retreats, leaving Konda's kingdom in ruins.

sok.text: Konda never once believes that he will lose the Kami War, as Masako recounts, and his daughter Michiko leaves home, promising not to return until she finds a way to bring him back to his senses.
When Konda arrives at Jukai and the Taken One summons O-Kagachi, Michiko and Kyodai merge and defeat the oni, and Konda is turned to stone and shattered.

neo.text: Daimyo Takeshi Konda builds Eiganjo Castle as a young man, drives out bandits and unites local warlords, but he later performs a sacrilegious ritual that breaks the barrier between the mortal and spirit worlds, imprisons a major spirit and gains immortality.
That crime triggers the Kami War, and the Myojin fall into chaos and turn against the material world.
At the climax of the war Konda and O-Kagachi are struck down by his daughters Michiko and Kyodai, and his immortal body is turned to stone and shattered into a thousand living pieces.
